features.feature_value: Used the pair to judge clarity/fairness; if either side seemed inflammatory or crude, removed both.
features.evidence_span: If there was responses on either side that seemed inflammatory or crude I said to remove them both
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes comparing both versions and applying an inflammatory/crude rule across either side.

features.feature_value: Removal triggered by hostile language, profanity, or being generally rude; claims not based on personal viewpoints.
features.evidence_span: remove posts that used hostile language or profanity, or were just rude in general. I did not consider my own personal viewpoints.
features.rationale: They specify concrete linguistic/behavioral criteria and note independence from personal views.

features.feature_value: Differentiated allowed opinions vs removed hate; seeing both sides helped them stay fair.
features.evidence_span: I allowed opinions. I removed hate. Seeing both sides helped me stay fair.
features.rationale: The participant gives a clear keep/remove contrast and attributes fairness to seeing both versions.

features.feature_value: Focused on harm/disinformation; even when only one post was problematic, it was still removed.
features.evidence_span: how harmful the posts were or how much disinformation was being spread
features.rationale: They define their content-based harm/disinformation lens and mention how the pair affected decisions even if only one item was problematic.

features.feature_value: Removed posts using hateful words while protecting free speech.
features.evidence_span: removed posts that used hateful words while protecting free speech.
features.rationale: They articulate a specific criterion (hateful words) paired with an explicit free-speech constraint.

features.feature_value: Chose based on which post seemed most reasonable to share.
features.evidence_span: I looked for the most reasonable post to share
features.rationale: Their decision logic is explicitly framed as selecting the most reasonable option from the paired materials.

features.feature_value: Wanted posters to tone down anger; some posts felt too inflammatory for practical discussion.
features.evidence_span: some of these posters need to tone down the anger... to inflmmatory to provide practical discussion.
features.rationale: They cite anger/inflammatoriness as a key cue influencing keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Evaluated whether comments advanced proper conversation versus devolving into rude namecalling.
features.evidence_span: Weather the comments pushed a proper conversation, or just rude namecalling
features.rationale: They describe a qualitative conversation-quality criterion tied to interpersonal tone.
